text:
Asha: running an ensemble-fallback canary (raven-lite int4 + raven-v2) and seeing parse flapping on funcall outputs when rate limits kick in. valid JSON one message, truncated/non-json the next. anyone seen this?
Noah: can you paste a tiny example of the alternating output?
Asha: repro log snippet below — it alternates between clean ndjson funccall lines and partial lines that break the parser :face_with_monocle:
```
2026-03-20T10:12:31.123Z INFO model=raven-lite tokens=+120 stream_chunk=1 output:
{"id":1,"tool":"search","args":{"q":"foo"}}
2026-03-20T10:12:31.145Z INFO model=raven-v2 tokens=+45 stream_chunk=1 output:
{"id":2,"tool":"lookup","args":{"k":"bar"}}
2026-03-20T10:12:31.198Z INFO model=raven-lite stream_chunk=2 output:
{"id":3,"tool":"summarize","args":{"t":"this is a lo"}
2026-03-20T10:12:31.250Z INFO model=raven-v2 stream_chunk=2 output:

2026-03-20T10:12:31.312Z INFO model=raven-lite stream_chunk=3 output:
"rest of text..."
```
Asha: those middle chunks are making the JSON parser raise halfway through the funcall array, then the retry budget tries the other model and we get a valid line again (so the stream alternates valid/invalid).
Ravi: hypothesis: ensemble fallback + strict streaming + rate-limit queuing => chunk boundaries line up with structural JSON tokens. essentially we’re getting interleaved partials from different replicas.
Ravi: quick checks: are we using continuous streaming across replicas or separate per-replica streams that get merged? if merged, that would explain interleaving.
Noah: looks like the router merges chunks as they arrive and forwards to client; we assumed per-request KV cache alignment would prevent interleaving but under RL rate-limit bursts we can get two concurrent stream producers for same logical request (fallback kicking in).
Ravi: quick mitigation to test: bump stream_chunk_buffer_ms to 200 and enable per-replica chunk boundaries (disable cross-replica merge) for canary. that will add a tiny latency but should reduce parse flapping.
Asha: I can flip config on canary 2 now. also adding a short NDJSON envelope sanity check before invoking structured parser so we can heal truncated suffixes w/ a 50ms wait + small retry.
eval-bot: experiment result (canary snapshot):
- baseline parse_failure_rate: 3.2% over 10k calls
- with stream_chunk_buffer_ms=200 + per-replica-boundary: 0.7% over 10k calls
- with envelope-sanity + 50ms heal only: 1.1%
Noah: nice. latency delta?
eval-bot: p95 latency increased from 84ms -> 98ms for those workloads (short-gen-focused). tokens cost unchanged.
Ravi: tradeoff seems acceptable for structured-funcall-heavy routes. also suggests adding a router-side guard: if chunk contains unbalanced braces/brackets less than X bytes from end, delay flush by Y ms (thermostat style).
Asha: rolling small patch to canary now (stream buffer + envelope-sanity). will monitor parse failure rate and regressions. ops-bot: deploy canary-asm-20260320 started by Asha at 10:16Z :rocket:
ops-bot: canary rollout step 1 -> 25% traffic (10:17Z), step 2 -> 50% (10:20Z)
Asha: initial telemetry at 10:22Z shows parse failures dropped to ~0.9% on canary shard, p95 latency stable within acceptable SLO. thumbs up :thumbsup:
Noah: can you add a tiny eval run that forces fallback under RL to verify behavior across different seq lengths? then we can formalize as a routing policy change.
Asha: will do, creating a short sampling eval and a ticket to make per-route stream buffering configurable. thanks all.
